r0.why: 'Brittle materials cannot be worked like that, so they may be cast or thermoformed' adds a causal link and says brittle materials cannot be stamped/pressed; [14] only contrasts with 'whereas' and [13] lists hammering/rolling/drawing/extruding, not stamping or pressing.

r1.why: Metallic bonds give high ductility [15]; delocalised shared valence electrons [16]; atoms slide without strong repulsion [17].

r2.why: Ceramics/semiconductors brittle [8]; rigid packed lattice [9]; restricts atom/dislocation movement [10],[11]; much smaller ductility at room temperature [12].

r3.why: Gold most malleable, platinum most ductile pure metal [21]; gold/copper ductile [5]; cast iron brittle [6]; steel alloying and carbon [18],[19].

r4.why: Plastics/Play-Doh malleable [20]; polymers ductile [7]; cold working suitability and overload absorption [3],[4].

r5.why: Length after vs before fracture [1],[2]; sample-dimension dependence [25]; factors of up to 2 or 3 [31]; toughness test preferable [35].
